headword: {高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}

definitions.explanation: Plants that grow naturally at high altitudes, typically above the tree line. They are adapted to harsh conditions including cold temperatures, strong winds, and intense sunlight.

examples.japanese: {高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}が{咲|さ}いている。
{高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}は{採取|さいしゅ}が{禁止|きんし}されている。
{夏|なつ}の{北|きた}アルプスでは{色|いろ}とりどりの{高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}を{楽|たの}しむことができる。
examples.english: In the Northern Alps in summer, you can enjoy colorful alpine plants.

notes:
Composed of {高山|こうざん} (high mountain) and {植物|しょくぶつ} (plants). In Japan, alpine plants are found primarily in mountain ranges such as the Japanese Alps and on mountains in Hokkaido.

Many Japanese {高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ} are protected and it is illegal to pick or transplant them. Mountain hikers are expected to stay on trails to avoid damaging them.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}のお{花畑|はなばたけ} (alpine flower meadow)
- {高山植物|こうざんしょくぶつ}を{観察|かんさつ}する (to observe alpine plants)
